decision.what: Route 3 (Now notices it is stale) over route 1 (swap the default view) or route 2 (Now shows newest cards, not newest owner thread)
decision.why: Route 1 is one line but does nothing for the exact person the bug report is about: `prefs` persists the owner's last chosen view, so anyone who has already landed on Now once keeps landing on Now regardless of what the default becomes. Route 2 is honest but changes what Now IS -- a single conversation thread becomes a recency feed -- and the brief is explicit that Now was built deliberately as the conversation view and a redesign is out of scope. Route 3 leaves Now's own shape untouched (still one heard card, still its answers) and only adds a notice when that heard card is not from today AND the board itself has something newer -- so a genuinely quiet day never false-alarms. The notice carries one obvious button, `Show today`, that switches the page's own view to timeline and saves it as the new preference, the same action the toolbar's own timeline tab already performs -- so a reader with no stored preference and a reader with `now` stored both land on a page that tells them, in one sentence, that they are looking at Friday and hands them one click to today.

harvest fix: the mastermind measured that after clicking Show today the view really switches to timeline and the preference really persists, but the toolbar tab strip kept reading now* because its `on` class was only ever painted once, at build time, in toolbar() - a pre-existing gap in the toolbar itself, not something introduced here, but only surfaced once go_timeline() gave the page a second way to change `view` besides a direct tab click. Fixed in public/framework/ai/v/3/page.js: toolbar() now records each view button in a `view_btns` Map (val -> $btn) as it builds them; a new `paint_view_tabs()` toggles the on class on every button in that map against the live `view` variable; `redraw()` - which every path that changes view already calls, both the toolbar clicks and go_timeline() - now calls paint_view_tabs() first thing. So the strip follows `view` no matter what changed it, not only a tab click. Nothing else touched - banner text, the Show-today button, persistence and the decision line are unchanged. node --check on the fixed file was refused again this session, same as before - could not run it.
